name: FWCP Annual Grants and Year-round Grants
summary: Grants to compensate for the impacts of BC Hydro dams on fish, wildlife and their habitat in the Coastal, Columbia and Peace regions of British Columbia. The 2026 annual intake closed November 2; year-round grants are no longer listed as open on the application page.

geography.label: BC Hydro dam watersheds, British Columbia

steps: Technical review, plus First Nations review in Columbia and Peace

eligibility.rule: Project aligns with one or more open priority actions
Applicant can provide a WorkSafe BC clearance letter and commercial general liability proof
Project is not a core activity of a government or non-government agency or program
Annual grant applicant is in good standing with FWCP
Annual grant project engages First Nations and documents that engagement
Project does not mitigate BC Hydro operating impacts covered by another program
Project does not carry out government enforcement or compliance activities
Land securement applicant can develop, fund and carry out a long-term conservation land management plan

documents: Mandatory letters of support for a Coastal Region project

applicant_types.quote: Eligible grant applicants include: First Nations government, communities, and businesses; consultants, agencies, non-government organizations, local governments, individuals, and academic institutions.

geography.quote: The FWCP was established to compensate for impacts to fish, wildlife, and their supporting habitat, resulting from the construction of BC Hydro dams.

access.quote: Who can apply for an FWCP grant? Eligible grant applicants include: First Nations government, communities, and businesses; consultants, agencies, non-government organizations, local governments, individuals, and academic institutions.

window.quote: What's coming in 2027: We're in the process of renewing our approach to project funding and will be implementing changes for our annual grant intake that opens in 2027.

effort.quote: Our 2026 annual grant intake closed November 2.
Stage 2: review by technical committees and First Nations Working Groups

Fish and wildlife technical committees in each region review each grant application for technical merit. In our Columbia and Peace regions, First Nations Working Groups also evaluate grant applications.

eligibility.quote: Your proposed project must align with one or more open priority action(s).
All grant applicants must be able to provide: a WorkSafe BC clearance letter; and proof of commercial general liability.
Core activities of government or non-government agencies or programs.
FWCP staff confirm the application is complete, the proponent is in good standing with the FWCP, and the project is eligible for funding.
Required engagement of First Nations in the proposed project: Document your engagement efforts in your grant application.

Projects to compensate for impacts to fish and wildlife resulting from the operation of a BC Hydro generating facility that has other programs in place (e.g., entrainment, ramping rates, water level changes, structural fish passage through a facility, or reservoir archaeology).
Enforcement and compliance activities under the purview of government agencies.
All FWCP-supported property acquisitions must be led by an organization with the capacity to develop, fund, and implement a long-term conservation land management plan.

after_award.quote: Final reports and a final statement of accounts are mandatory for all FWCP-funded projects.

documents.quote: A six-page (maximum) project proposal is required for all annual grant applications. Letters of support Include mandatory letters of support for your project in our Coastal Region.
